title: A reproducible infection protocol for entomopathogenic nematodes in the natural host Plodia interpunctella larvae
author: Mallick, Chakkalakkal, et al.

steps.title: Prepare standardized larval diet
steps.instruction: Weigh 10–12 mg of Plodia interpunctella eggs into a weighing boat and transfer them to a rearing container containing 45–50 g wheat bran diet supplemented with 30 % glycerol; maintain under uniform environmental conditions to obtain third‑instar larvae.

steps.title: Set up infection petri dishes
steps.instruction: Use 30 Greiner Bio‑One Petri dishes (35 × 10 mm; USA Scientific). With a sterile spatula place a single third‑instar larva into each dish, taking extreme care not to harm the insect. Allocate ten dishes as uninfected controls (add 50 µL sterile water to each control larva) and twenty dishes per nematode species for infection.

steps.title: Surface‑sterilize infective juveniles
steps.instruction: Suspend the infective juveniles (IJs) in 1 mL sterile water in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, centrifuge at 13,000 rpm for 10 s at room temperature, discard the supernatant, add 1 mL freshly prepared 1 % bleach solution and gently mix. Wash the pellet five times with 1 mL sterile water each, then resuspend the final pellet in sterile water to obtain a suspension containing 500 IJs per 50 µL.

steps.title: Inoculate larvae with nematodes
steps.instruction: Pipette precisely 50 µL of the IJ suspension (500 IJs) onto each designated larva, ensuring the nematodes are in direct contact with the larval body.

steps.title: Seal and incubate dishes
steps.instruction: Secure each petri dish with non‑airtight laboratory adhesive tape applied around the lid to prevent larval escape while allowing airflow. Place the dishes in a 25 °C incubator with a 12 h light : 12 h dark photoperiod (all experiments were performed at 28 °C, 60–80 % relative humidity).

steps.title: Monitor larval survival
steps.instruction: Observe larvae at two‑hour intervals; record death when a larva shows no reaction to gentle poking with a pipette tip. Perform three biological replicates, each comprising twenty infected larvae and ten uninfected control larvae.

steps.title: Analyze survival data
steps.instruction: Use GraphPad Prism to generate Kaplan‑Meier survival curves and compare groups with the Log‑rank (Mantel‑Cox) test; median survival times may be compared using Welch’s unpaired t‑test.
